identity.title: Position: The AI Imperative: Scaling High-Quality Peer Review in Machine Learning

problem.claim: Machine-learning peer review is strained by rapidly increasing submissions, with finite qualified-reviewer capacity raising concerns about quality, consistency, and fatigue.

gap.claim: The paper identifies a need for AI-assisted review systems and for more granular, structured, ethically sourced peer-review process data to develop them.

contributions.claim: Argues that AI-assisted peer review should become an urgent ML research and infrastructure priority.
Advocates an AI-augmented ecosystem in which LLMs collaborate with, rather than replace, human authors, reviewers, and Area Chairs.

Proposes AI roles spanning factual verification, reviewer guidance, author quality improvement, and Area Chair decision support, alongside illustrative experiments and discussion of technical and ethical challenges.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a comprehensive AI-augmented peer-review ecosystem and associated research agenda centered on collaborative LLM assistance and process-data access.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that submission growth at premier ML venues is outpacing qualified-reviewer capacity and is associated with concerns about review quality, consistency, and reviewer fatigue.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames ML peer review as facing a scale crisis.
Calls AI-assisted peer review an urgent research and infrastructure priority.
Positions LLMs as collaborators for authors, reviewers, and Area Chairs rather than replacements for human judgment.
Specifies assistance roles, emphasizes granular and ethically sourced process data, and outlines illustrative experiments plus technical and ethical challenges.
Calls for proactive development that preserves scientific validation integrity and review standards while improving scalability.

source_observation.claim: The paper pairs a multi-stakeholder system proposal with an explicit data requirement and a validation agenda, while preserving human judgment as a constraint.

lessons.interpretation: This linkage can make a position paper more actionable by connecting roles, prerequisites, and evaluation needs.
lessons.application: For a proposed sociotechnical system, map each stakeholder role to required data and illustrative validation studies, and state which human decisions remain authoritative.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the work addresses a narrowly scoped technical component without meaningful stakeholder roles or process-level dependencies.

unknowns: The abstract does not report results from the proposed illustrative experiments, specify system designs or datasets, or provide evidence that the proposed assistants improve review outcomes.
The abstract does not identify a specific limitation of existing AI-review approaches beyond the stated scaling and data-access needs.
